```sh
git clone git@github.com:bar9/yolo-twice.git
cd yolo-twice/code
bun install          # all workspaces, about 2 s
bun run build        # core, analyzers, engine, pele-markdown, then the UI, about 10 s
bun test             # 22 tests, about 2 s
bun run typecheck
```

Start the engine for this repository and open the UI:

```sh
bun run cli open --cwd ..      # starts the daemon if needed, prints and opens the URL
bun run cli status --cwd ..
bun run cli stop
```

The repository ships its own `.yolo-twice/` folder, so even on a machine that never ran a
session here the UI shows the committed history. To continue that session in Claude Code:

```sh
bun run cli resume --cwd ..    # rebuilds the transcript under ~/.claude and runs claude --resume
```

## Running the plugin from your checkout

Two options, pick one.

**Per session, nothing installed.** Claude Code loads the plugin straight from the folder:

```sh
cd /path/to/yolo-twice
claude --plugin-dir code/plugin
```

**Installed, the way users get it.** Register your checkout as a local marketplace once.
Edits to the plugin files take effect in new sessions:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add /path/to/yolo-twice
claude plugin install yolo-twice@yolo-twice
```

Inside Claude Code the command is `/yolo-twice:yolo-twice`, with `stop`, `status`,
`mode <detent>` and `resume [id]`. The plugin's launcher finds the engine in your checkout,
so it runs your local code. It prefers `code/packages/engine/dist/cli.js` when present, so
run `bun run build` after changing engine code, or delete `dist/` to fall back to running
the TypeScript source with bun.

Hooks post to `127.0.0.1:9656`. When the engine is down they fail silently, so a session
without the engine is never disturbed.

To remove the dev install:

```sh
claude plugin uninstall yolo-twice@yolo-twice
claude plugin marketplace remove yolo-twice
```

## Where the code lives

| Path | What | Inner loop |
|---|---|---|
### Engine

Run it in the foreground from source so logs go to your terminal:

```sh
bun run engine -- --cwd ..
```

Useful environment variables:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `YOLO_TWICE_PORT` | port instead of 9656, so a dev engine can run next to an installed one |
| `YOLO_TWICE_HOME` | runtime state folder instead of `~/.yolo-twice` |
| `YOLO_TWICE_NO_LLM=1` | never call `claude -p`; summaries come from the structural fallback |
| `YOLO_TWICE_ORIGIN_DIR` | `index` reads sessions from this folder instead of `~/.claude/projects/<slug>` |
| `YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE` | the plugin launcher runs this engine (a `cli.js`, a `cli.ts` or a command) |
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | where Claude Code's data lives, if not `~/.claude` |

A fully isolated dev engine that cannot collide with anything installed:

```sh
YOLO_TWICE_HOME=/tmp/yt-home YOLO_TWICE_PORT=9661 YOLO_TWICE_NO_LLM=1 bun run engine -- --cwd ..
```

Stop the npx engine that's holding port 9656, then start the engine from source in `code/`. The hooks always post to port 9656, so whichever engine owns that port is the one that receives your sessions.

## 1. Free port 9656

The engine you have running now came from npm (started with `npx`) and is watching `/home/bar9/testing`. Stop it:

```sh
npx yolo-twice stop      # or: kill 815368
```

## 2. Build and run from source

```sh
cd /home/bar9/yolo-twice/code
bun install
bun run build
bun run engine -- --cwd ..     # runs in the foreground, logs go to your terminal
```

To start it in the background instead and open the UI, run `bun run cli open --cwd ..`.

## 3. Make `/yolo-twice:yolo-twice` use your checkout

Without this step, the slash command can start the npm engine again. Your installed plugin is 0.1.0 from the GitHub marketplace, so it doesn't know where your checkout is. Pick one fix:

- **Per session:** start Claude with `claude --plugin-dir code/plugin` from the repo root.
- **Permanently:** switch the marketplace to your local folder:
  ```sh
  claude plugin uninstall yolo-twice@yolo-twice
  claude plugin marketplace remove yolo-twice
  claude plugin marketplace add /home/bar9/yolo-twice
  claude plugin install yolo-twice@yolo-twice
  ```
  The launcher then uses `code/packages/engine/dist/cli.js`. Run `bun run build` after you change engine code. If you delete `dist/`, it runs the TypeScript source with bun instead.

## Running a test engine alongside the real one

If you want to try out engine changes without disturbing the engine that records your sessions, run a second one on another port with its own state folder. With `YOLO_TWICE_NO_LLM=1` it never calls `claude -p`:

```sh
YOLO_TWICE_HOME=/tmp/yt-home YOLO_TWICE_PORT=9661 YOLO_TWICE_NO_LLM=1 bun run engine -- --cwd ..
```

These steps come from `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the "Running the plugin from your checkout" and "Engine" sections).

== bin/yolo-twice
#!/bin/sh
# Run the yolo-twice engine CLI. Resolution order:
#   1. $YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE  (path to cli.js, or a command)
#   2. repo dev layout next to this plugin (code/packages/engine)
#   3. a marketplace clone under ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/*/code/packages/engine (built on first use with bun)
#   4. npx -y yolo-twice@latest
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CMD="${1:-open}"; [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
case "$CMD" in
  stop|status|index|start|open|mode|resume|hook|help) ;;
  micro|attentive|balanced|yolo) set -- "$CMD" "$@"; CMD=mode ;;
  *) set -- "$CMD" "$@"; CMD=open ;;
esac

run_engine_dir() {
  dir="$1"; shift
  if [ -f "$dir/dist/cli.js" ]; then exec node "$dir/dist/cli.js" "$@"; fi
  if command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$dir/src/cli.ts" ]; then
    if [ ! -d "$dir/../../node_modules" ]; then (cd "$dir/../.." && bun install >/dev/null 2>&1); fi
    exec bun run "$dir/src/cli.ts" "$@"
  fi
  return 1
}

if [ -n "${YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE:-}" ]; then
  case "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" in
    *.js) exec node "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" "$CMD" "$@" ;;
    *.ts) exec bun run "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" "$CMD" "$@" ;;
    *) exec "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" "$CMD" "$@" ;;
  esac
fi
if [ -d "$HERE/../packages/engine" ]; then run_engine_dir "$HERE/../packages/engine" "$CMD" "$@"; fi
CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
for d in "$CLAUDE_DIR"/plugins/marketplaces/*/code/packages/engine; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && run_engine_dir "$d" "$CMD" "$@"
done
# marketplace added from a local directory (dev install): its path is recorded in known_marketplaces.json
if [ -f "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/known_marketplaces.json" ]; then
  for p in $(grep -o '"path": *"[^"]*"' "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/known_marketplaces.json" | sed 's/.*"path": *"//; s/"$//'); do
    [ -d "$p/code/packages/engine" ] && run_engine_dir "$p/code/packages/engine" "$CMD" "$@"
  done
fi
exec npx -y yolo-twice@latest "$CMD" "$@"

else

fi

I'd keep the plugin version in step with the engine version and have CI enforce it. For the cached copy, I'd change nothing and just know when you need to reinstall.

## 1. Version mismatch: sync it and enforce it

**Bump `code/plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to 0.1.2 and change it in every release commit from now on.** This matters more than the label: Claude Code stores the installed copy in a folder named after the version (`cache/yolo-twice/yolo-twice/0.1.0`). If the version never changes, `/plugin update` may decide nothing is new and keep the stale copy. Both of today's release commits (`bba1a4b`, `cc8429c`) changed only the engine's `package.json`, which is how the two versions drifted apart.

**Add a check to CI so they can't drift again.** `publish.yml` already fails when the git tag doesn't match `package.json`. One more line can fail the build when `plugin.json` doesn't match either:

```sh
p=$(node -p "require('../../plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json').version")
[ "$p" = "$v" ] || { echo "::error::plugin.json $p != package.json $v"; exit 1; }
```

The other packages (core, analyzers, ui, pele-markdown) can stay at 0.1.0. They're bundled into the engine and never published separately.

## 2. Cached plugin copy: mostly leave it alone

**Engine changes are already live.** The cached launcher finds your checkout through `known_marketplaces.json`, so after a `bun run build` the new engine code runs. That's where nearly all your changes will happen.

**Only edits under `code/plugin/` need extra steps.** Those files are the hooks, the slash command and the launcher scripts, and they rarely change. When you do edit them:
- **To try a change:** start a fresh session with `claude --plugin-dir code/plugin`, which loads the plugin straight from your folder.
- **To make it stick:** bump the version (see section 1), then run `/plugin update`, or uninstall and install again.

I'd add one row about this to the troubleshooting table in CONTRIBUTING.md, something like "plugin edits not showing up → the install is a copy; reinstall or use `--plugin-dir`". There's already a similar row for the engine's `dist/` folder.
